question: Why is fentanyl citrate short, and what do we do?

steps.title: Our stock in three hospitals
steps.purpose: Read on-hand stock and 28-day use where each hospital keeps it.
steps.finding: 7 stock lines across 3 hospitals, 2 presentations, in units of use.

steps.title: Where our supply is made
steps.purpose: Follow each product's label to the plants it names, and place each plant in FDA's registration file.
steps.finding: 2 plant links on 2 labels; 2 placed in FDA's registration file.

steps.title: What FDA says about this shortage
steps.purpose: Read FDA's current shortage list and its history for this drug.
steps.finding: On FDA's list as Current for 3 companies.

steps.title: Who else makes it

steps.finding: 5 labelers make it in this form.

steps.title: What FDA found at those plants
steps.purpose: Read every FDA drug inspection, warning letter, import alert and recall for these plants.
steps.finding: 48 inspections (3 OAI at our plants), 2 compliance actions, 0 import-alert listings, 0 recalls.

steps.title: What FDA wrote at the OAI inspections
steps.purpose: Read the Form 483 observations recorded at those inspections.

steps.title: What our P&T committee already approved
steps.purpose: Read Corvale General's approved interchanges for these items.

steps.title: Which links can't be trusted
steps.purpose: Run the semantic layer's key rules (NDC and unit of use) over each hospital's stock, and name the rows they reject.
steps.finding: 11 stock rows across the system fail the NDC rule; 0 of them are this drug. Every row is in a shared unit of use.

explanation.headline: FDA's shortage list shows fentanyl citrate injection current since 2012-01-01 for Hospira and Fresenius Kabi, and since 2023-12-20 for Hikma; no FDA action at a registered plant precedes the earliest posting

sentences.text: FDA's shortage list records fentanyl citrate injection as current for Hospira, Inc. (a Pfizer Company) with an initial posting date of 2012-01-01 and an update date of 2026-10-08.
The same list shows Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC as current with an initial posting date of 2012-01-01 and an update date of 2026-10-15.
Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc. appears as current with an initial posting date of 2023-12-20 and an update date of 2026-10-14.
FDA's database start date is 2012-01-01, so the shortage began on or before that date and no gap is measured from it.
Hikma's registered plant (FEI 2220525) has only VAI inspections, the latest ending 2024-06-12 with a known date of 2024-12-16, and its label shows last inspection NAI 2026-05-13.

The rule-based best option is to transfer 74 syringes of 50 ug/mL, 1 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East, which would raise Corvale East from 5.6 days to 10 days on hand while Corvale General retains two weeks of supply.

rejected.text: Hospira's registered plant (FEI 1021343) received OAI classifications in 2010-01-19, 2011-06-17, and 2011-08-04, all after the 2012-01-01 posting, and its most recent inspection was NAI on 2025-02-07.
rejected.reason: date 2012-01-01 is not in the cited evidence

memory.text: Decision on lidocaine: switch lidocaine 1% 30 mL vials to 5 mL vials in the ED to reduce waste during the shortage. Rationale: Single-dose waste was a third of use (demo history). Approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD.

Decision on carboplatin: move the primary carboplatin contract from Accord to Teva and keep Accord as secondary. Rationale: Accord's supplier plant had an FDA warning letter; Teva supply steadier (demo history). Approved by Riley Brooks, PharmD.
